clue.text: Spoke tartly and caused a split

definitions.meaning: to speak sharply and irritably at someone
broke something cleanly in two with a crack

explanation.surface: Someone's sharp words drove a wedge between friends.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share one word: a curt retort and a sudden break, as of a twig.

clue.text: Resort to telephone to effect saving

parts.note: a spa is a health resort
to ring is to telephone

explanation.surface: Calling to book a holiday to cut costs.
explanation.definitionFit: Being economical with money or resources means using little.

clue.text: The American army's revolutionary command

parts.note: the US drill order to turn round and face the opposite way

explanation.surface: An order from the army of the American Revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' suggests the War of Independence, but it means turning round; British drill says 'about turn'.
explanation.definitionFit: The parade-ground order to turn to face the opposite direction.

clue.text: Newsmen cause harassment

definitions.meaning: to pressure or harry someone persistently

explanation.surface: Reporters pester people.
explanation.definitionFit: Journalists collectively are the papers' people, and to pester is to bear down on someone.

clue.text: Despair at being made to appear contrary

indicators.note: the letters are made to appear in another arrangement

explanation.surface: Gloom made to look like its opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being made to appear' rearranges DESPAIRAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Things fundamentally unlike or opposed to each other are dissimilar or contrary.

clue.text: There's drink left — keep up!

parts.note: to sup is to drink in small mouthfuls
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: A bar-room call to a flagging companion: there's still a drink waiting, so hang on.
explanation.walkthrough: PORT for 'left' comes from sailing: the left-hand side of a vessel facing forward.
explanation.definitionFit: To support something is to hold it up, a synonym of keep up.

clue.text: Considering, a point in church

parts.note: S, south, is a point of the compass
taken as written
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Reflecting on a doctrinal point raised in church.
explanation.definitionFit: As a conjunction it means because or seeing that, i.e. considering.

clue.text: Silly saps without the game needed by travellers abroad

indicators.note: without means outside, so the anagram goes round the other piece
silly means the letters of the word are jumbled

parts.note: sport is a game

explanation.surface: Foolish people left without a game, pondering what overseas visitors require.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Silly' turns SAPS into PASS, which goes 'without' (outside) SPORT: PAS-SPORT-S.
explanation.definitionFit: Travellers crossing borders must carry official identity documents.

clue.text: There's nothing, nothing whatever, like an egg

parts.note: O, the figure nought, means nothing
a void is complete emptiness

explanation.surface: A remark that nothing resembles an egg so closely.
explanation.definitionFit: Egg-shaped, from the Latin word for egg.

clue.text: A climbing frame for use in the garden

definitions.text: A climbing frame for use in the garden

parts.words: A climbing frame for use in the garden
parts.note: not a children's play frame but a lattice that climbing plants grow up

explanation.surface: Play equipment for children in the back garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing frame' suggests children, but it is the plants that climb.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooden or metal lattice that supports climbing plants such as roses.

clue.text: Give satisfaction, being in accord

definitions.meaning: make amends or reparation for a wrong
split as two words, ... means agreeing completely

explanation.surface: A peacemaker settles a quarrel by reaching agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the answer into AT ONE, meaning in agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: Making amends is giving satisfaction for an offence, and being at one is agreement.

clue.text: One stands out for such building material

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of the two words are put out of their order

explanation.surface: A single item that stands out among the materials for a building project.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges ONESTANDS into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A sedimentary rock quarried and cut into blocks for walls and houses.

clue.text: Not willingly late

parts.note: late means dead, and 'not willingly' means without having made a will

explanation.surface: Someone who arrives late but not on purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Late' is the obituary sense, deceased; 'willingly' hides 'will', the legal document, so the dead person left no will.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who dies without a valid testament has died in this legal state.

clue.text: Go by foot

definitions.meaning: to ride a bicycle, working the cranks with the feet
as an adjective, of or relating to the foot

explanation.surface: A plain instruction to walk.
explanation.walkthrough: The verb is cycling, and the adjective is the anatomical term for things of the foot, as in a foot pulse.
explanation.definitionFit: A cyclist travels by working the cranks, and the anatomical adjective describes things of the foot.

clue.text: Beastly food offered by Greek simpleton

parts.note: an ass is a foolish person

explanation.surface: A dull-witted Greek serves up a meal fit for animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Grazing cattle and sheep eat this pasture plant, so it is food for beasts.

clue.text: The missile-launcher for Which support's enthusiastic

parts.note: a sling supports an injured arm; the 's adds S
hot means keen or eager

explanation.surface: Keen backing for a weapon-launching device.
explanation.definitionFit: A forked stick with elastic for firing stones, a missile launcher.

clue.text: Sounds like freebooters!

parts.note: as means like, in the sense of in the manner of
freebooters are pirates or plunderers

explanation.surface: An exclamation that some noise resembles a band of pirates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sounds like' looks like a homophone signal, but 'Sounds' is the definition and 'like' gives AS.
explanation.definitionFit: In phonetics these are breathy h-sounds, so they are kinds of speech sound.

clue.text: To deal with only one part is bad

indicators.note: bad means the letters are in a bad, corrupted order

explanation.surface: Handling just a single section is wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' rearranges ONEPARTIS; 'only' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To give one's custom to a shop is to trade or deal with it regularly.

clue.text: The people included in the list can be located

indicators.note: one word is included in another, sitting inside it

parts.note: a table is a list of data
a race is a people

explanation.surface: Names on a register can be tracked down.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that can be tracked or found is able to be located.

clue.text: Trips need to be well organised for the chief executive

indicators.note: being well organised means the letters are arranged afresh into a new order

explanation.surface: A head of state's travel arrangements must be carefully planned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be well organised' rearranges TRIPSNEED into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In a republic the head of state, or of a company, holds the top executive office.

clue.text: Speaks well of produce in addition to writing

indicators.note: in places the word for produce inside the abbreviation

parts.note: PS, postscript, is an addition to a letter
to raise is to produce, as crops or children

explanation.surface: Commending farm produce and literary work alike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'produce' is a verb here, not farm goods.
explanation.definitionFit: To commend or applaud is to speak well of someone.

clue.text: A note quickly written

definitions.meaning: a musical symbol or pitch a semitone raised

explanation.surface: A brief memo dashed off in haste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'note' means a written message on the surface, but here it is a musical note.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical pitch raised by a semitone, and promptness as in 'look sharp'.

clue.text: Huff about bond being invalid

indicators.note: about means one word goes round the other

parts.note: to huff is to pant, breathe heavily
a tie is a bond

explanation.surface: Anger over a contract declared void.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invalid' is the noun, a sick person, not 'void'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sick person under care is an invalid.

clue.text: Flying can be scary

definitions.meaning: on the wing, in flight, an old poetic phrase

explanation.surface: Air travel can frighten nervous passengers.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as A-WING it means in flight; read as one word it is the present participle of 'awe', frightening.
explanation.definitionFit: On the wing describes a bird in flight, and something that fills you with awe is daunting.

clue.text: Grabbing an animal that's to be put out

indicators.note: grabbing means one piece seizes and holds the other inside it

parts.note: i.e., id est, means that is
a rat is an animal

explanation.surface: Seizing a creature that is to be ejected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' means annoyed, not ejected.
explanation.definitionFit: Being put out is being annoyed or angry.

clue.text: Important men in port maybe

indicators.note: maybe suggests the letters could be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: Distinguished men can perhaps be found at a harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' rearranges MENINPORT into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Standing out and well known, as a leading figure is.

clue.text: The man's in very poor shape — terribly ill

annotationWithheld.why: The man's in very poor shape — terribly ill (5) for PETER: no parse found giving PETER from these words.
annotationWithheld.clue: The man's in very poor shape — terribly ill

clue.text: Mixing paint can be awkward

indicators.note: mixing means the letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Blending colours can be clumsy work.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsuitable or clumsy, ill-fitting for the situation.

clue.text: Get this wound up before eating

definitions.text: Get this wound up before eating

parts.words: Get this wound up before eating
parts.note: the long strands of a pasta dish are twirled round a fork before each mouthful

explanation.surface: Someone is told to wind something up before a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wound up' suggests winding a clock or annoying someone, but it is twirling pasta round a fork.
explanation.definitionFit: Long thin Italian pasta strands are wound on a fork to be eaten.

clue.text: Move the beer when the medico comes in!

indicators.note: the medico comes into the word for beer, sitting inside it

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A call to shift the drink before the doctor arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Move' is the definition, in the sense of walking at a leisurely pace.
explanation.definitionFit: To stroll is to walk slowly, a gentle way to go along.

clue.text: Scatter these about left and right for protection

indicators.note: scatter means the letters are spread about and regrouped

explanation.surface: An instruction to strew some things around on both sides as a safeguard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scatter' (with 'about' reinforcing it) rearranges THESE plus L and R.
explanation.definitionFit: A refuge or cover gives protection from weather or danger.

clue.text: Implore a certain character to discuss terms

parts.note: an en is a printer's measure, the width of one typeset character
to treat with someone is to negotiate

explanation.surface: Begging a particular person to negotiate a deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treat' in the old sense of negotiate, as in a treaty.
explanation.definitionFit: To beg earnestly is to implore.
